name: Raspberry Pi 5
frame: Pi 5 lying component side up (+z up, USB-C and HDMI on the -y front, USB and Ethernet on +x, power button and microSD on -x): tests a snap case that clears nine ports and controls on three walls, with heights from Raspberry Pi's own STEP because the drawing gives none.
open_why: faces whose features the maker does not locate, or that must stay clear, as the spec's why says: Pi 5 lying component side up (+z up, USB-C and HDMI on the -y front, USB and Ethernet on +x, power button and microSD on -x): tests a snap case that clears nine ports and controls on three walls, with heights from Raspberry Pi's own STEP because the drawing gives none.

board.why: the PCB's underside is 1.45 mm above the body's -z face, the bottom of the microSD socket (STEP RP-010083 bbox z -1.45); a part must hold the board there on standoffs, not under the socket

features.name: power_button
features.source: https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rpi5/raspberry-pi-5-mechanical-drawing.pdf and https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/892-raspberry-pi-5/documents/RP-010083-CA-1-rpi-5%203D%20STEP%20-%20No%20Graphics%20small%20file.zip: y: drawing left edge '18.4' from the front board edge (u = 57.63 - (18.4 + 1.63)); the '0.45' overhang on the drawing is this part. v and size: STEP RP-010083 body bbox x -0.45 to 0.6, y 17.4 to 19.4, z 2.036 to 4.036. Naming it the power button is mine: the drawing does not label it; plug: Ø10, our number, a lower bound and not the size of a finger. MIL-STD-1472F, https://www.denix.osd.mil/soh/denix-files/sites/21/2016/03/02_MIL-STD-1472F-Human-Engineering.pdf Figure 12 'Push button (finger or hand operated)', p73, gives 'MIN 10 mm (0.4”)' as the least diameter of a button pressed with a bare fingertip; that sizes the button, not the opening a finger reaches through, and a fingertip is wider. The button sits 2 to 3 mm in behind the case wall, so an opening narrower than this cannot let any fingertip reach it
